\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{اختبار} (ikhtibār)}{اختبار (ikhtibār)}]{\ar{اختبار} (ikhtibār) — a test}

\label{lesson:AR-C393-ikhtibar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a supervisor, then the Arabic for to study for.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{اختبار}}
\textbf{\ar{اختبار}} — \emph{ikhtibār} — \textquotedblleft{}a test\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{نجحت} \ar{في} \ar{اختبار} \ar{القيادة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{najaḥtu fī ikhtibār al-qiyāda.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I passed the driving test.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{اختبار}} (\emph{ikhtibār}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{kh-b-r}, \textquotedblleft{}to know thoroughly, to test\textquotedblright{} (Lane). \emph{Ikhtibār} is the Form VIII verbal noun of \emph{ikhtabara}, to test: a test.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ikhtibār}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ikhtibār}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{najaḥtu fī ikhtibār al-qiyāda.} — I passed the driving test.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a supervisor, then the Arabic for to study for, then say \emph{ikhtibār} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{اختبار} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A test\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{قبول} (qabūl)}{قبول (qabūl)}]{\ar{قبول} (qabūl) — admission}

\label{lesson:AR-C393-qabul}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to study for, then the Arabic for a test.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{قبول}}
\textbf{\ar{قبول}} — \emph{qabūl} — \textquotedblleft{}admission\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{حصل} \ar{أخي} \ar{على} \ar{قبول} \ar{من} \ar{الجامعة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ḥaṣala akhī ʿalā qabūl min al-jāmiʿa.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My brother got admission from the university.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{قبول}} (\emph{qabūl}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{q-b-l}, \textquotedblleft{}to be in front; to receive\textquotedblright{} (Lane). \emph{Qabūl} is a verbal noun of \emph{qabila}, to accept: acceptance, admission.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{معدل} (muʿaddal)}{معدل (muʿaddal)}]{\ar{معدل} (muʿaddal) — an average}

\label{lesson:AR-C393-muaddal}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a test, then the Arabic for admission.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{معدل}}
\textbf{\ar{معدل}} — \emph{muʿaddal} — \textquotedblleft{}an average\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{معدل} \ar{أختي} \ar{ممتاز} \ar{هذه} \ar{السنة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{muʿaddal ukhtī mumtāz hādhihi as-sana.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My sister's average is excellent this year.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{معدل}} (\emph{muʿaddal}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ʿ-d-l}, \textquotedblleft{}to be equal, straight\textquotedblright{} (Lane). \emph{Muʿaddal} is the Form II passive participle, made even: an average, a rate.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{muʿaddal}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{muʿaddal ukhtī mumtāz hādhihi as-sana.} — My sister's average is excellent this year.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a test, then the Arabic for admission, then say \emph{muʿaddal} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{تفوق} (tafawwaqa)}{تفوق (tafawwaqa)}]{\ar{تفوق} (tafawwaqa) — to excel}

\label{lesson:AR-C393-tafawwaqa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for admission, then the Arabic for an average.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{تفوق}}
\textbf{\ar{تفوق}} — \emph{tafawwaqa} — \textquotedblleft{}to excel\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{تفوق} \ar{ابن} \ar{جارنا} \ar{في} \ar{الرياضيات}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tafawwaqa ibn jārinā fī ar-riyāḍiyyāt.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Our neighbour's son excelled in mathematics.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يتفوق}, \emph{yatafawwaq}.

It takes \ar{في} for the field, and \ar{على} for the people one beats.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{تفوق}} (\emph{tafawwaqa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{f-w-q}, \textquotedblleft{}to be above\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form V, to rise above others: to excel. \ar{فوق}, above, is from the same root.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tafawwaqa}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tafawwaqa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tafawwaqa ibn jārinā fī ar-riyāḍiyyāt.} — Our neighbour's son excelled in mathematics.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for admission, then the Arabic for an average, then say \emph{tafawwaqa} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{قيم} (qayyama)}{قيم (qayyama)}]{\ar{قيم} (qayyama) — to evaluate}

\label{lesson:AR-C393-qayyama}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for an average, then the Arabic for to excel.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{قيم}}
\textbf{\ar{قيم}} — \emph{qayyama} — \textquotedblleft{}to evaluate\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{قيم} \ar{المعلم} \ar{عمل} \ar{كل} \ar{طالب}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{qayyama al-muʿallim ʿamal kulli ṭālib.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The teacher evaluated each student's work.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يقيم}, \emph{yuqayyim}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{قيم}} (\emph{qayyama}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{q-w-m}, \textquotedblleft{}to stand, to rise\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form II, to set a value on a thing: to evaluate. \ar{قيمة}, a value, is from the same root.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{qayyama}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{qayyama al-muʿallim ʿamal kulli ṭālib.} — The teacher evaluated each student's work.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for an average, then the Arabic for to excel, then say \emph{qayyama} again
\end{itemize}
